neighbours.label: The imagined or perceived scene in a small clause after 'imagine', 'picture' or 'see' (the object plus its '-ing' action: 'imagine your family sitting…'), not the same '-ing' action outside a perception or imagination frame.
fire: Try to imagine your grandparents dancing at their wedding.
I can still picture my father fixing the old car in the yard.
Many children imagine dragons flying over their houses at night.
She closed her eyes and imagined herself standing on the stage.
From the window we saw the deer crossing the frozen lake.
It is hard to picture the city filled with horses and carts.
He liked to imagine the soldiers marching through the valley.
Readers can easily picture the two friends arguing in the kitchen.
quiet: My grandparents danced at their wedding until midnight.
My father fixed the old car in the yard every summer.
Many children are afraid of the dark at night.
She stood on the stage and waited for the music.
The deer crossed the frozen lake before dawn.
The city was filled with horses and carts back then.
The soldiers marched through the valley in the rain.
The two friends argued in the kitchen for an hour.

notes: Probes (fraction of max 17.88): 'imagine your family sitting around' 0.566, 'imagine cats sleeping on soft cushions' 0.509, 'picture myself walking' 0.284, 'saw the bird landing' 0.254. The same actions without the frame: 'spent the afternoon walking' 0.011, 'The bird was landing' 0.030, 'know that cats sleep' 0.013. Peak tokens vary within the small clause.
